title: The line he kept on his phone

The line he kept on his phone

He gave one sentence out of a two-page report, and it worked anyway.

linkedin:
The client had been in and out of gyms for a decade. He knew the language: progressive overload, macro splits, and every one of them had failed to survive a work trip.

The coach sent the usual report. The client responded with a thumbs up and, as far as anyone could tell, never opened it again.

The coach asked him, a week later, to screenshot one line from it — whichever one he'd keep.

The client sent back this: your training hasn't failed, your weeks have changed eleven times since January and the plan never changed with them.

He'd photographed it. It was on his phone.

The lesson isn't that the report should be one line. It's that a document earns its place by containing at least one sentence a person can carry. Everything else is reference material.

When a coach writes the note, that's the sentence to aim for.

MOJOWAY's kit puts the coach's own note at the top for exactly this reason: the data supports it, but the sentence is what the client keeps.
